title: hetero-coldstart-rebalancer-and-weighted-warmup-scaler
author: Evan Park
release_notes: Introduce a heterogenous coldstart rebalancer and a weighted warmup scaler to reduce cross-tenant cold-start tail latency. Backwards-compatible, opt-in via benchmark-values helm flag.
description: Motivation: In our multi-tenant benchmark clusters we observe repeated coldstart-induced tail spikes when traffic lands on under-warmed replicas across heterogeneous GPU families. Existing warmup runners treat replicas uniformly and do not account for heterogeneous priming costs, leading to unnecessary token-generation waste and uneven KV cache states. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a lightweight daemon (hetero-coldstart-rebalancer) that continuously scores replicas by a 'coldstart_score' derived from recent warmup history, model variant, and device priming cost, and issues prioritized warmup tasks; (2) a weighted warmup scaler/runner that performs progressive prefix priming with configurable weight profiles so expensive replicas receive fewer, higher-impact priming sequences while cheap replicas receive broader short priming. Design and changes: - bench/rebalancer/daemon.py: new daemon that subscribes to bench coordinator events, computes coldstart_score, and enqueues warmup jobs with priorities. - bench/warmup/weighted_runner.go: new runner implementing configurable weight schedules (linear, exponential, step) and KV-checkpoint-aware priming to avoid redundant KV fills. - scheduler/priority_warmup_hook.cc: scheduler hook enabling priority injection without stalling normal serving queues (non-blocking). - bench/reports/rebalancer_exporter.py: compact exporter that emits new metrics (coldstart_score, warmup_progress, priming_efficiency) and compact trace events for the reporting pipeline. - helm/benchmark-values.yaml: new feature flag benchmarks.heteroColdstart.enabled (default false) and tunables for weight profiles. - docs/bench/rebalancer.md: design doc and rollout notes. - tests/integration/test_rebalancer.py: integration test with mocked device cost profiles and synthetic traffic to validate prioritization and warmup convergence. Implementation notes: - The daemon uses an EWMA over warmup success and recent traffic to compute coldstart_score; scores are device-cost-normalized so that the scheduler prefers priming cheaper replicas first unless warmup_progress lag exceeds a threshold. - Warmup runner supports deterministic prefix sequences from the canonical seed corpus used by the bench lab to keep priming reproducible across runs. - Exporter attaches compact trace spans for each queued warmup and a small summary blob to the existing bench telemetry sink to avoid increasing cardinality. Test plan and results: - Unit tests added for scoring logic and weight schedules. - Local integration runs across a 3-node hetero cluster (A100, A10G, T4-equivalent) using the lab multi-runner harness. Observed improvements: median coldstart completion time per cohort reduced by ~33% and p95 reduction of ~22% on synthetic small-priming workloads; overall warmup token consumption reduced ~18% for the sampled runs. Rollout plan: - Feature gated off by default. - Canary deploy to benchmark-lab perf cluster in eu-west-1 for 48h, monitor warmup_progress and priming_efficiency. - If metrics stable, enable on all bench clusters and schedule a broader cluster roll. Checklist: - [x] daemon, runner, exporter implemented - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs and helm flag - [x] perf smoke and benchmark comparisons - [x] telemetry labels and dashboard draft - [x] reviewers sign-off (see approvals below)
